# Embed Images in Markdown

> A VS Code extension that embeds images into Markdown as DataURLs, just by dragging and dropping.

Embed Images in Markdown is a Visual Studio Code extension. While a Markdown file is open, holding `Shift` and dragging an image file (`png`, `jpeg`, `jpg`, `gif`, or `webp`, extensions case-insensitive) onto the editor converts the image to a DataURL and inserts it into the file. A reference link is placed at the drop position, and the DataURL-encoded image body is appended to the end of the file. This keeps a Markdown document and its images self-contained in a single `.md` file, with no separate image assets to manage.

It also supports dragging image files from the VS Code Explorer view, and pasting into an inactive editor pane when multiple panes are open.

## Requirements

- Visual Studio Code version 1.74.0 or higher.
- The setting `markdown.editor.drop.enabled` must be set to `false` for the extension to work.

## Known limitations

- If multiple files are dragged and dropped at the same time, only one is pasted.
